inputs.share_count_basis: Issued shares excluding treasury: 243,114,557 x 10 = 2,431.1m at the 2026-06-11 AGM buy-back mandate (H1 FY2026 interim report), less 807,600 treasury shares; cross-checks to the H1 dividend base (RMB461.8m / RMB0.19 = 2,430.5m). Includes the RSU-trust shares (the 2,406.5m weighted basic count excludes unvested contingently-returnable shares), so this is the fully diluted count. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The May-2025 80m-share top-up placing is already in the count; no further non-SBC issuance modelled.
inputs.cash_composition: 30-Jun-2026 interim balance sheet (RMB'000): cash and equivalents 1,492,354 + term deposits >3m current 3,578,113 + non-current 2,049,571 + FVTPL wealth-management products 150,276 + debt instruments at amortised cost 68,577 = 7,339.0m. Debt: borrowings 1,760,779 (current, working-capital loans; secured plant loans only 10.8m) + lease liabilities 7,664 + 9,283 = 1,777.7m.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income was RMB204.8m in FY2025, but only RMB23.9m ('Interest received', FY2025 AR cash-flow statement line 6097) sits inside OCF; term-deposit interest is collected through 'redemption of term deposits' in investing and is therefore not in reported FCF. Deducting the full 204.8m would strip interest that was never in the FCF base. The component build is struck at EBITDA excluding finance income, so all interest is out of the projected flows; the deposits that earn it are in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR: share-based payments RMB15.789m (statement of changes in equity / cash-flow add-back); no net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every period). H1 FY2026 SBC was a net reversal of RMB5.4m. FY2022 excludes the RMB628.8m one-off pre-IPO award.
inputs.buyback_note: Effectively a non-repurchaser: HK$3.6m bought back in H1 FY2026 (507,600 shares) under the June-2026 mandate; FY2021 RMB1.8bn was a pre-IPO restructuring repurchase. The flat count is a modelling convention, but SBC is so small (~0.2-0.6% of revenue) that the difference is immaterial. Capital is returned by dividends (~90% payout incl. specials).
inputs.fx_note: Statements in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1744 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-23 (regularMarketTime 1792792707); inverse check HKDCNY=X 0.8507 -> 1/0.8507 = 1.1755, a 0.1% tie confirming direction. No dual listing for a price-parity check. All values computed in CNY and converted to HKD; unsuffixed per-share values are HKD.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% CNY cost of capital, all-equity (the company is net cash; the 1.76bn of borrowings is short-term working-capital debt held against 7.3bn of deposits). China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta ~0.85 x China ERP ~7.0% = ~7.8%, plus ~1.2pp for the HK-listed PRC private-company governance/capital-control discount. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried in the flows, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): lease liabilities (RMB16.9m) included once in total_debt; no lease charge in the flows (lease_cost_pct 0). Principal repayments are RMB5-12m/yr, immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is RMB9.3m of equity (30-Jun-2026) with a small loss share in H1 FY2026; flows are consolidated and the NCI book value is deducted once in the equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, via make build-dcf. Routing: Weilong is an operating consumer-products manufacturer (latiao seasoned flour products, konjac/kelp vegetable snacks) selling through offline distributors and growing online direct sales; no banking, property or holdco features, so the 'operating company, non-US' row applies with the adaptations (RMB flows/HKD quote, leases, NCI, deposits-as-cash with their interest stripped). First valuation of this ticker - no MEMORY.md entry. Analysis.json was not yet written when this build ran; scenario axes are drawn from the filings (H1 FY2026 interim: seasoned flour -9.8%, vegetable +15.8%, online +43.8%, offline +2.7%, net margin 21.1% -> 20.6%). FY0 is FY2025 revenue; the balance sheet is the later 30-Jun-2026 interim, so H1 FY2026 cash generation (FCF RMB49.6m after the seasonal contract-liability unwind) is already in net cash - a negligible overlap. The RMB0.19 interim + RMB0.09 special dividend (RMB680.5m) declared for H1 FY2026 is payable ~26-Oct-2026; the share price is already ex-entitlement (the ~HK$0.33 dividend lines up with the late-September drop), so the cash is deducted in the equity_bridge. Adjusted EBITDA here = operating profit before finance income + D&A + SBC: FY2025 1,853.3 + 170.3 + 15.8 = 2,039.4 (28.2% of revenue); H1 FY2026 est. 27.1% vs 29.5% in H1 FY2025 - selling costs rising faster than the 0.6pp gross-margin gain.

equity_bridge.item: H1 FY2026 interim RMB0.19 + special RMB0.09 dividend declared, payable ~2026-10-26 (price is ex)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 9.7% is >30% below the 16.0% revenue 3yr CAGR: the company pays out ~90% of profit (incl. specials), so book value understates operating growth. Revenue 3yr growth was itself flattered by the FY2022 trough (-3.5%); FY2025 revenue growth was 15.3% and H1 FY2026 only 6.7%. EPS 3yr CAGR omitted: FY2022 EPS 0.07 is depressed by the RMB628.8m one-off pre-IPO SBC charge.
historical_growth.notes: Only FY2021-FY2025 annuals exist (listed Dec-2022), so 5yr CAGRs are null and 4yr CAGRs from FY2021 are shown instead. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest received inside OCF (25.3/55.2/24.0/23.9). The owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (9.7%) exceeds the reported FCF CAGR (5.8%) because SBC fell from 98m to 16m - the opposite of the usual warning. FY2021 owner FCF (~446m) is excluded from the CAGRs: it was a pre-IPO capex-heavy year.

base.narrative: Konjac (Mo Yu Shuang) keeps compounding low-double-digits and online direct sales scale, while latiao shrinks mid-single-digits as offline traditional-channel traffic erodes; group growth settles ~6% then fades to 3%. EBITDA margin eases from 28.2% (FY2025) to ~26.5% as online and brand spend outgrow the supply-chain gross-margin gains already visible in H1 FY2026. Capex steps down from the FY2025-26 plant build (5.5-5.8%) to ~3.3%.

bull.narrative: The new-product engine works: stinky tofu and further vegetable/low-burden SKUs become a third leg, latiao stabilises after the resource reallocation, overseas localisation adds a growth line, and the online/snack-discount channels (Busy Ming, Snack Lovers) keep growing with scale economics. Revenue reaccelerates to ~10% and margin recovers to the FY2025 high and edges above it on procurement and digital cost savings.

bear.narrative: Konjac follows latiao's path: copycats and the bulk snack-discount chains commoditise the category, so the vegetable line (66% of revenue) turns down while latiao keeps falling with offline traffic. Revenue shrinks ~12% cumulatively over FY2026-29 before stabilising at ~1.5% growth; deleverage, konjac raw-material inflation and a price war take EBITDA margin from 28.2% to 21%. This is the case the late-2026 halving of the share price is pricing.

scenario_narratives.base: Konjac keeps compounding and online direct sales scale while latiao shrinks with offline traffic; ~6% growth fading to 3%, EBITDA margin easing 28.2% -> 26.5% as channel and brand spend outgrow supply-chain savings; capex normalises after the plant build. Net cash (RMB5.6bn after the payable dividend) is ~40% of the market cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: New categories (stinky tofu, low-burden vegetable SKUs) and overseas become real growth legs, latiao stabilises, the snack-discount and e-commerce channels keep scaling; revenue reaccelerates to ~10% and margin returns to and slightly above the FY2025 high.
scenario_narratives.bear: Konjac commoditises under copycats and discount-channel price pressure while latiao keeps falling; single-category dependence (vegetable products 66% of H1 FY2026 revenue) produces a ~12% revenue decline over four years, margin down ~7pp to 21%, then ~1.5% growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the core latiao line is already shrinking (-9.8% in H1 FY2026), two-thirds of revenue now rests on one category (konjac) with low barriers to imitation, and offline traditional-channel traffic is falling. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs both new-category success and margin recovery. Base 50%. The balance sheet (net cash ~40% of market cap) removes any solvency tail, which is why bear is not higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A highly cash-generative, net-cash Chinese branded snack maker paying out ~90% of earnings. The value question is the durability of konjac growth against a shrinking latiao franchise, not the balance sheet. Flows are owner FCF built from components at a 9% CNY rate; deposits are added at book with their interest stripped from the flows; the declared-but-unpaid H1 dividend is deducted because the price is ex.
key_risks_to_valuation: Category concentration: vegetable (konjac) products are 66% of revenue and growing on a low-barrier product
Latiao decline accelerating with offline traditional-channel traffic
Margin compression from online/discount-channel mix and brand spend (H1 FY2026 EBITDA margin ~2.4pp lower YoY)
Food-safety event in a category with a history of regulatory scrutiny
Capital allocation: cash held in RMB deposits with short-term borrowings alongside; HK-listed PRC governance and capital-control discount
CNY/HKD rate: values are converted at a dated spot rate that refresh_price.py does not update
